summary: Google Products flicker is not confirmed or cleared by frame-by-frame pixel evidence (QA-002).

summary: No constraint validation before submit: a form with an empty required field or a malformed email/number submits and sends the bad value.
evidence: BR-105. Proof of the old state and the fix: docs/tasks/TASK-031-FORM-SUBMISSION-CORRECTNESS.md §7 (Mutation proof [R-7]); internal/engine/forms.go ValidateForm and the pre-submit check at internal/engine/engine.go:1623-1630. Engine oracles live in test/engine/form_submission_test.go; the browser-level oracle cmd/goosie/journey_p1_form_validation_test.go:TestJourneyFormValidationBlocksRequestUntilValid asserts an invalid submit leaves the server at page:1 search:0 with the URL unchanged.

summary: <select> has no node in the accessibility tree, so an assistive user cannot see or operate the control at all - even though TASK-030 made it keyboard-operable.
evidence: BR-139. Measured while writing the BR-101 journey: the layout arena carries obj tag="select" id="sel", Session.AccessibilityTree() under the form returns only role=4 id="send"; cmd/goosie clickNode therefore cannot address a select (journey uses clickElementByID). Recorded in docs/tasks/TASK-030-SELECT-INTERACTION.md §9.4. Closed on 910c445 (feature 3c16f37). Oracles: test/engine/accessibility_test.go:TestAccessibilitySelectComboBoxAndOptions and :TestAccessibilitySelectTracksMoveSelect, both tagged // qc:BR-139, plus internal/platform/darwin/ax_role_test.go pinning the AppKit role codes. The integrator re-ran all five mutations on the branch and each one turned the feature off, then passed again on revert: emitter removed (combo missing), every option marked selected ("selected options = 3, want exactly 1"), combo value read from the select's value attribute ("combo value = \"\""), selectedness computed by index instead of the attribute ("Label:One ... want Two/two" after MoveSelect), and RoleComboBox mapped to GROUP ("maps to 1, want GOOSIE_AX_COMBO_BOX (12)"). cmd/goosie/journey_p1_forms_test.go:TestJourneySelectOptionChange now reaches the control through clickNode, i.e. through the accessibility tree, instead of clickElementByID. Disclosed: VoiceOver itself was never exercised - the darwin oracle asserts the role code, not what a screen reader says, so mutation (v) of the task spec has no behavioural test.

summary: ::first-line is not supported at all, so a first-line colour or weight is silently dropped. (The original attribution of selectors/03's three blank bands to missing ::first-letter/::first-line support is falsified - see evidence.)
evidence: BR-075. Registered by TASK-027 as 'the residual is the missing first-letter/first-line support'. Two of those three causes no longer hold, and one never did. (1) ::first-letter is implemented: 2f1519d 'feat(layout): implement ::first-letter pseudo-element drop cap box (BR-075)', merged 5978371. testdata/render-known-gaps.json declared selectors/03-pseudo-elements.png at 3 blank regions before that commit (git show 2f1519d^:testdata/render-known-gaps.json) and still declares 3; re-measured at 452b6c2 the same three bands remain, at the identical rows (457,475) (539,554) (579,599). Implementing ::first-letter removed none of them. (2) Those three bands are not missing content at all: Goosie paints the lines, ~20px away from Chromium's band rows, so the blank test fires on vertical drift. For band (457,475) Goosie has ink rows 437-455 and 483-498 and none in between, and the crop shows 'This paragraph has a checkmark after it' rendered with its checkmark. See GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001. (3) What is genuinely unsupported is ::first-line, measured directly on 2026-10-26: a one-rule page 'p.fl::first-line{color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold}' at 400x200 renders 1,043 red px in Chromium (computed color rgb(255, 0, 0)) and 0 red px in Goosie, all 544 of its ink px black. Priority lowered P1 -> P2 on this measurement; the ::before/::after content in the same fixture renders, and the residual band count is an artifact of the metric, not of this defect.

summary: Colour emoji still draw as tofu: golang.org/x/image/font/opentype does not read sbix/COLR tables.
evidence: TASK-027 killed 8 of the 9 blank bands in unicode/02-emoji-symbols.png; the remaining band at rows (451,470) is Chromium's Apple Color Emoji line box (~26px) versus Goosie's 18px tofu line, i.e. cumulative vertical drift, not a missing glyph. Note added to docs/roadmap-v2.md. TASK-027 round 2 merged at 6074040: candidates are ordered by measured coverage, a face is admitted only when its cmap covers the rune, coverage is memoized per candidate path, and the 4 MiB ceiling is checked by os.Stat before ReadFile. Measured over whole ranges instead of samples: 364 non-CJK code points across 8 scripts, 358 resolve, and exactly 6 miss - U+03A2 (Greek), U+063B-U+063F (Arabic) - which the oracle now declares as gaps in both directions. CJK stays tofu on this host by admission design: every system CJK face is over the ceiling (Arial Unicode 22.2 MiB, STHeiti 55.7, Songti 66.9, PingFang ~50-80), so colour-emoji and CJK coverage remain the open half of this defect. The 6 Greek/Arabic code points are unrenderable by any admitted host face under the ceiling and are not tracked separately.

summary: TestNativeEndToEndPlaysARealVideo is load-sensitive: under a busy machine it can time out, which risks a false red in the sweep's gate step.
evidence: test/engine/media_native_test.go:264. Observed while running full suites in parallel worktrees; TASK-029 §3 forbids raising the timeout as a fix, so it is recorded here instead. Same class observed on 2026-10-25 at 20:07: TestFootprintAtRestIsBoundedByConfiguredCaches reported retained=257.03 MiB against configured=207.10 MiB while 14 orphaned busy-loop shells from an old stress command held the 1-minute load average near 90; the identical run passed at 2.29s on the same commit (130bc9a) once the load was removed. The at-rest footprint criterion is therefore load-sensitive and must be measured on an idle machine, never in parallel with another suite.

summary: Button-level formnovalidate is not honoured: a submit button carrying formnovalidate still runs constraint validation, so the 'Send without saving' pattern cannot submit an incomplete form.
evidence: grep -rn formnovalidate internal/engine returns no matches, while the merged bypass oracle test/engine/form_submission_test.go:TestFormNovalidateBypass only exercises the form-level novalidate attribute. WHATWG HTML 4.10.13.3.6 step 9 collects and honours the submitter's novalidate state; ValidateForm (internal/engine/forms.go) reads only the form attribute.

summary: Browser-level tests read the layout arena from the test goroutine, so the journeys that decide whether a feature works are unsynchronised against the engine's input goroutine.
evidence: 14 sites in cmd/goosie/*_test.go walk sess.Arena.Objects directly (cmd/goosie/e2e_test.go:188 clickElementByID, clipboard_test.go:36,121, form_nav_test.go:58,130,251, ...). TASK-030's -race run proved the same class of cross-goroutine DOM read is unsafe, and the locking contract requires locked Session accessors. A mutation that rebuilds layout can therefore produce a torn read or an unsynchronised click coordinate instead of a clean failure.

summary: The tab scroll-restore journey asserts a cross-tab inequality instead of an exact offset, so it can pass for the wrong reason or fail when both tabs clamp to the same scroll extent.
evidence: cmd/goosie/journey_p1_tabs_test.go:96-105 presses PageDown twice in tab 2 and waits for active.ScrollY() > tab1Scroll, comparing one tab's offset against a different tab's; the same test then asserts exact equality (== tab1Scroll, == tab2Scroll) at lines 121 and 132. The inequality oracle depends on page heights and clamp values, and it is the assertion that failed twice under machine load.

summary: 103 of the 161 P0/P1 QA cases still have no tagged test, so most of the manual catalogue remains unverified automatically even though every P0 case is now tagged.
evidence: test/qc/traceability.golden.json at 910c445: 185 cases, P0 19/19 tagged, P0+P1 161 cases of which 58 tagged, so 103 P1 cases have no tagged test. Split by catalog method: 73 carry only machine-checkable methods (INT/PARITY/SEC) - BR-139 was one of them until TASK-032 tagged it, 13 pair CUA with a machine method, and 17 are labelled CUA-only - but docs/tasks/TASK-035-CHROME-STATE-ZOOM-AX.md §1 measured that BR-126/127/128/129/130/131 of that last group already ship real app paths (cmd/goosie/toolbar_window.go:286-290 disabled flags and the Stop label swap, cmd/goosie/interaction.go:648-657 clampZoom) and are assertable through the accessibility tree, so CUA-only overstates how much must stay manual. scripts/rc-sweep.sh:117-119 fails only when a P0 case loses its test or the count falls below docs/qa-ratchet.json, so the untagged majority is invisible to the gate.

summary: The parity harness can report success while its own evidence shrinks: --no-strict deletes fixtures from the denominator, and the known-gaps baseline is an upper bound (<=), so inflating it hides blank bands instead of exposing them.
evidence: BR-176/BR-177. Measured by importing testdata/parity.py (importlib) against a one-fixture temp corpus, leaving the real /tmp render dirs untouched: declared baseline 5 with 0 measured blank bands yields ('a.png', 'PASS', 100.0, [], 5, None); deleting the chromium render under strict=False yields [] - the fixture vanishes from the report, so N/N (100%) and rc 0. strict=True does report MISSING ('chromium render missing') and a missing gaps file raises FileNotFoundError, so the fail-closed half exists; what is missing is any floor on the number of scored fixtures and any check that a declared band baseline still equals what is measured. grep shows no script, Makefile or CI target passes --no-strict, and every entry in testdata/render-known-gaps.json currently matches its measured band count exactly (2/2, 1/1, 3/3, 1/1, 3/3 at 4437f65), so an equality gate is satisfiable today.

summary: A select's submitted value is raw option text content and the first selected option wins, so Goosie sends whitespace the server never sees from Chromium and resolves multi-selected markup to the wrong option.
evidence:
BR-101/BR-104/BR-106/BR-139. Measured on this host: Goosie submitted name="c" value="
  Charcoal
" for an option whose text content is '
  Charcoal
' and encoded it as c=%0A++Charcoal%0A, while Chromium/Playwright normalises the same shape to option.textContent = '  Hi
  there
' -> option.value === 'Hi there' (strip plus internal whitespace collapse). For a <select> with two selected options Chromium reports selectedIndex 1, value 'b', formdata 'b' (last wins) whereas SelectedOption (internal/engine/focus.go:634) returns the first. The accessibility tree trims option labels (internal/engine/accessibility.go:172) but the combo Value comes from controlValue untrimmed, so one control announces a different string than it submits. All four blocked cases already have tagged tests that pass today (BR-101 7 tests, BR-104/BR-106 one journey each, BR-139 3 tests) - none asserts the normalised value or the tie-break, so this defect hides behind green tests, not behind a missing test. Optgroup is out of scope: internal/engine/select.go:46-48 records that options nested in an optgroup are unreachable.

summary: Seven P1 chrome/session cases (BR-043/044/045/049/054/055/056) had no tagged test at all, so visit-log ordering, forward-trail discard, session cursor restore and private-mode isolation were trusted entirely to manual QC.
evidence: test/qc/traceability.golden.json at 4437f65 lists tests: null for all seven. d61403d (merged at f53be0c) tags one oracle per case. Integrator re-ran everything rather than trusting the report: go test -count=1 ./... FULL-RC=0 including test/gate and test/gatecheck; -race on cmd/goosie, test/tabs, test/history rc 0; go vet -all ./... rc 0; go test ./test/qc/ -update followed by empty git diff (golden idempotent, and still idempotent after the merge). Seven behaviour-off mutations were reproduced by hand, each killing its own test: consecutive-repeat guard (Entries() = 2 records, want 1), Push forward-truncation ([a b c d]@3, want [a b d]@2), private opening profile stores (private app stores/client = ... want client and no profile stores), private journalling (session_active.json exists after close plus regular startup found a private crash journal containing https://private.example/secret), private jar not cleared (private jar after Close = [{Name:Y ...}]), failed load recorded (history after failed load has 4 entries, want 3), and dropped history cursor (5 assertions red in TestSessionStateRoundTrip). All reverted; git status clean and no MUTATION-TEMP residue. An extra integrator probe found the per-tab incognito case is already pinned: dropping the !tab.Incognito() guard at cmd/goosie/navigation.go:319 fails the pre-existing TestIncognitoHistorySuppression. Disclosed limits: one oracle per case, and the failed-load fixture uses a connection-refused URL rather than an HTTP 500 page, so the error-page branch of that rule is untested.

summary: On nine real web pages Goosie lays out nothing, or paints a handful of pixels, and still exits 0 with an empty stderr - the user gets a blank window and the engine records no reason anywhere.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-001. Measured by testdata/live-parity.py against Chromium/Playwright at viewport 1280x1024, dpr 1, wait_until=load, screenshots viewport-only on both sides. Source: docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json (94 of 100 pages comparable). Eight pages have doc_height=0 AND ink_goosie=0 with goosie_rc=0 and an empty goosie_diag: apnews.com (Chromium painted 15,805 ink px), www.nytimes.com (68,129), www.japantimes.co.jp (17,749), www.reuters.com (13,145), www.etsy.com (16,539), www.newegg.com (17,467), www.zara.com (8,846), www.gov.vn (501,735). vnexpress.net is a different shape of the same silence: doc_height=691 but ink_goosie=32 against ink_chromium=301,440. All nine carry the identical label in the earlier run (2026-10-25T1630Z) as well, so this is not load noise; of the 6 label changes between the runs none is in this family (www.usatoday.com was LAYOUT_EMPTY at run 1 and LOW_COVERAGE at run 2, so it is deliberately not counted here). Offline probes on saved copies of the served HTML prove this is at least two distinct causes, not one: www.gov.vn reproduces with no network (curl-saved 192,815-byte document whose decoded text carries 11,859 visible characters across 177,201 body characters, served with 26 inline <script> tags) and ./bin/goosie -screenshot on that file yields rc 0, ink 0, while -gate -frames 120 reports doc_height=0, tiles_rasterized=0, zero_work_frames=120 - the frame path ran 120 frames with no document to draw. apnews.com does NOT reproduce offline: the same command on its saved 2,610,822-byte copy (70,685 visible characters) paints 763,855 ink px at doc_height=34,867, so the live failure of that page must come from the fetch/response path rather than from layout of the markup. (www.gov.vn is also the only page in this family whose corpus expect is 'static'; the other seven are 'js-revealed'.) Caveat for whoever investigates: style_passes and layout_passes read 0 on both runs, including on apnews where layout clearly succeeded, so those two counters are frame-window figures and must not be cited as evidence that styling never ran. Nothing distinguishes any of these from a page that genuinely has nothing to draw: the -screenshot path exits 0, so neither CI nor a user can tell. Not root-caused further - TASK-038 §4 forbids engine changes in a measurement task.

summary: A legal custom property name that begins with digits (--8e8e8e) is mistaken for an oversized geometry dimension, so the whole document is refused: cafef.vn gets no window, and the message names no property, no value and no limit.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-002. Reproduced offline with no network from a saved copy: ./bin/goosie -screenshot -url file:///tmp/cafef.html (217,170 bytes) exits 1 and writes exactly one stderr line, 'goosie: goosie: build session: CSS numeric value outside safe geometry range' (the prefix is doubled). The live sweep labels it ADMISSION_CAPPED in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json; in the earlier run it was GOOSIE_CRASH, the same family mislabelled before the ladder put a refusal check ahead of the exit-code check. ROOT CAUSE, measured by bisection and not yet fixed: document -> 9 <style> blocks (dropping them clears the refusal; dropping style= attributes does not) -> block 8 of 36 rules -> one rule, '.box-ttdn .list .mdn .time { color: var(--8e8e8e, #8e8e8e); ... }'. The one-line repro is ':root{--8e8e8e:#8e8e8e}' and '.a{color:var(--8e8e8e)}'. The name of that custom property begins with digits, so the tokenizer reads 8e8 as a scientific number and then swallows the following 'e8' as a unit, producing a Dimension token worth 800,000,000; internal/engine/limits.go:239-241 applies MaxGeometry = 2<<20 (2,097,152) to dimensions and percentages, and the document is refused. A variant matrix measured on this host confirms the mechanism exactly: ':root{--8e8:1}' rc 0 (plain number, cap deliberately skipped), ':root{--8e8e8:1}' rc 1, ':root{--1e9e9:1}' rc 1, ':root{--8e5e5:1}' rc 0 (800,000 under the cap), ':root{--1e2e2:1}' rc 0, ':root{--abc8e8e8:1}' rc 0 (ident, no number token), '.a{width:8e8}' rc 0, '.a{width:8e8e8px}' rc 1 (a genuine dimension, correctly refused). Chromium, measured with Playwright on the same minimal document, resolves var(--8e8e8e) to rgb(171, 205, 239): a custom property name that begins with digits is legal and contains no number at all, so this refusal is a false positive that blanks an entire news site - renaming the one ident to --grey makes the saved cafef document render at rc 0 with 554,999 ink pixels. Hypotheses already disproved on this document: replacing every 7-or-more-digit number (including z-index:999999999) does not clear the refusal, because the trigger is an 8-character ident with no run of digits; and the document loads no external stylesheet, so linked CSS is not involved. Compounding the damage, the same coarse message is emitted from three sites - internal/engine/limits.go:226 (float64 overflow), :231 (non-finite), :241 (magnitude) - and none names the property, the value, or the bound, unlike :249 'CSS declaration limit exceeded (%d)'.

summary: A -screenshot run that gave up at its hard-coded 25 s deadline is indistinguishable from one that settled: same exit code, same PNG, no field that says 'not settled'.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-003. cmd/goosie/drive.go:170 sets steadyDriver's deadline to 25 * time.Second, and :241 ends the wait with 'if d.settledFn == nil || time.Since(started) >= d.deadline' - returning as though the run had completed. Nothing marks the difference: no stderr, nonzero exit, or field in the artifact. Measured headroom on the 2026-10-25 corpus: the slowest Goosie render was 8.93 s (www.straitstimes.com), then 7.70 s (www.noaa.gov) and 6.66 s (dw.com), so no page in this sweep reached the deadline - the gap is unexercised here, not proven harmless. The harness had to work around it by timing each render itself and inventing a NOT_SETTLED label (testdata/live-parity.py classify, selftest case 'slow'); any other consumer of -screenshot has no such signal. Changing the constant is out of scope for a measurement task (TASK-038 §4), which is why it is registered rather than tuned.

summary: The parity scorer can grade a page 'OK' while Goosie's ink sits almost nowhere near Chromium's: coverage is an ink-mass ratio that rises above 1, and the positional score (worst_iou) is recorded but never consulted.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-004 - a defect in the measuring infrastructure, not in the engine. coverage comes from parity.score_regions (testdata/parity.py:279): goosie_total / chromium_total, so it exceeds 1 whenever Goosie paints more ink than the reference. 30 of the 94 comparable pages in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json report coverage > 1.0, up to 2.83 (www.w3.org/Style/CSS/, 1,306,325 Goosie ink px vs 15,209 Chromium), 2.57 (ebay.com, 1,228,884 vs 94,816), 2.32 (validator.w3.org). Worse, the label ignores position: among the 46 OK pages, 26 have worst_iou < 0.5 and 16 have worst_iou < 0.1, including en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam (coverage 1.547, worst_iou 0.001, 0 of 4 bands blank) and wiki/Cuneiform (1.972, 0.014). grep of testdata/live-parity.py shows worst_iou is written at :162 and never read by classify. Written on 2026-10-25 as: 'blank-band and dimension checks are position-sensitive, so LAYOUT_EMPTY, BLANK_OUTPUT, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH stay trustworthy'. That half is now falsified for BLANK_OUTPUT: measured on 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2, a band reported blank can hold Goosie's line ~20px away (GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001), so BLANK_OUTPUT does not by itself prove content is absent. LAYOUT_EMPTY, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH are unaffected by that measurement and still stand. What is missing is a positional criterion that separates 'content absent' from 'content elsewhere'. Disclosed rather than retuned: LIVE_COVERAGE_OK = 0.60 and MIN_SCORED = 75 were fixed before the first run and never adjusted afterwards (TASK-038 §6.5).

summary: An unterminated string in a stylesheet is never turned into a CSS bad-string token, so Goosie swallows the rest of the sheet and paints it on the page as generated content.
evidence: Root cause: internal/css/token.go:201-240 readString() loops until it finds the matching quote and writes every other byte, newline included, so it consumes to end of input and returns TokenString. CSS Syntax Level 3 4.3.7 requires a bad-string token at the newline, which invalidates and drops the declaration. grep -rn 'bad-string' internal/ returns nothing. Minimal repro, one rule 'content: """;' on a .q::before: Goosie paints '"""; font-size: 48px; color: #3498db; } .q { font: 16px monospace; color: #000; }' in 48px blue text before the paragraph, 8,424 ink px; Measured at a matched 1280x1024 canvas on both sides: Goosie 2,845 ink px vs Chromium 523 - 5.4x the reference, all of it stylesheet source. (Goosie's default -screenshot window is 2880x1800 and paints 8,424, which is why the canvas is pinned.) Chromium computes content: none for the same pseudo. The .q rule after the bad string never applies either - 'Hello world' shows in the default serif - so the whole remainder of the sheet is lost, not just one declaration. The corpus fixture already has it: testdata/render/selectors/03-pseudo-elements.html:47 and :53 both read 'content: """;', present since 2bea5cc which added the fixture set. At 800x2400 Goosie paints 68,830 ink px with the string broken and 49,295 after replacing it with 'content: "\201C"' (Chromium 59,068), i.e. ~9.8k px of raw CSS on the page. Invisible to every current gate for two independent reasons: at the scored 800x600 viewport the broken and fixed renders have byte-identical ink (28,719 px each) because the leak is below the fold, and score_regions builds its bands from the Chromium mask only, so Goosie ink where Chromium has none is never examined. Pre-existing, not a TASK-033 regression: git diff 4de0fca HEAD -- internal/css/token.go is empty.

summary: The ::first-letter admission rule is written three times and the incremental-restyle copy has no oracle: gutting it leaves the whole suite green.
evidence: Three copies of one rule. internal/style/pseudo.go:37-56 (resolvePseudoElements) and internal/style/pseudo.go:91-105 (reResolvePseudoSubtree) carry the identical 'before/after/first-letter' loop and the identical 'cs.Content != "" && cs.Content != "none"' admission test; the third decision is in internal/layout/arena.go:498-512. The re-resolve copy has none of the comment that explains the first one (pseudo.go:47-51, why content:"" must still generate a box for clearfixes), so whoever edits one copy will not know why the other exists. reResolvePseudoSubtree is reachable only from internal/style/incremental.go:157, i.e. the hover/restyle path. No oracle covers it: test/layout/first_letter_test.go:246 TestFirstLetterIncremental asserts only WorkCounts().LayoutBuilds deltas (:279 must not change, :295 must change by 1) - that a rebuild happened, never what style or box the rebuilt first-letter got. Measured at 452b6c2: replacing the first-letter branch inside the reResolvePseudoSubtree copy so it admits nothing left go test ./... green (mutation M2 survived), which also breaks the [R-7] rule that every oracle needs a positive expectation. Not a user-visible defect today - the copies agree - so P2: it is an uncovered-code and silent-divergence risk on the path users reach by hovering.

summary: A global inline-layout float skip shipped inside the ::first-letter commit changes float layout on real pages, is not needed by that feature, and no test fails when it is removed.
evidence: internal/layout/inline.go:387 - 'if k.Node == nil || k.Style == nil || k.Style.Display == style.DisplayNone || k.Style.Float != style.FloatNone' sits in inlineInto's generic child loop, so it drops every floated child from inline collection everywhere. git blame: the clause is from 2f1519db (2026-10-25, the ::first-letter commit); the rest of the line is db4bedff (2026-09-17). It is not first-letter specific and the feature does not need it. Scope measured 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2 by deleting the clause, rebuilding, and re-rendering all 80 corpus fixtures at 800x2400 with both binaries: exactly one fixture differs - layout-features/05-floats.png, 51,447 px of symmetric ink difference - and the other 79 are pixel-identical. At the scored 800x600 viewport the same change is 162 px and the fixture passes either way, so make parity cannot see it at all. On that fixture at 800x2400 the parity numbers flip hard: worst_iou 0.6866 -> 0.0000, coverage 0.9813 -> 0.9474, blank bands 0 -> 1 (Chromium band rows 1055-1071 cols 20-460 holds 2,775 ink px; Goosie holds 0 with the clause and 2,289 without). Those numbers do not prove the clause is wrong: the line 'Content after the overflow:hidden container (should be below).' is painted in both variants, about 15px apart, so the band goes blank from vertical drift (GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001), not from lost content. What is proven is that it is uncovered: removing it failed no test in go test ./... (mutation M3 survived). Decision owed by the owner: either add a float test that fails without the clause and say which spec rule it implements, or drop it from the feature and land it separately with that test.

summary: A 'blank band' in the parity metric can mean 'Goosie painted that line 20px away', not 'content missing', so the known-gaps baseline counts and TASK-027's band classification are not evidence about features.
evidence: testdata/parity.py:253-279 score_regions(): bands come from content_bands(cm) on the Chromium mask only, and a band is reported blank when goosie_count == 0 inside Chromium's exact rows.
